transcripts.transcript: Everyone is talking about AI these days, some people say it's a new technological wonder but others seem worried about it. However, it's not always easy to know what it is and what it really means to you. If you search for it online, you might even get an answer provided by AI. As you may already know it stands for artificial intelligence. The term refers to a field in computer science for creating systems with some level of autonomy to generate recommendations, texts, images or sounds based on human interactions. Currently, most AI systems adopt machine learning techniques where computers are taught on how to behave based on large amounts of data and statistics. Artificial means something that does not exist in nature but is created by people usually to copy something natural and these artificial systems are made to automate tasks to copy human behavior. However AI is not intelligent, it is a tool trained to repeat some behaviors. Airplanes were created inspired by the behavior of birds, but they cannot make nests, sing, reproduce and do other amazing things birds can do the same goes for AI. It mimics a few human behaviors and can be very helpful with some tasks. But it doesn't come close to the full complexity, autonomy and intelligence of human beings. That is why behind every system lies human action from the engineers who design them to the people who creates meaningful information to train them. Many AI systems work with neural networks which are inspired by how neurons connect to each other in our brains. These networks have interconnected nodes to process and analyze large amounts of data, splitting it into small parts. So machines can perform tasks like recognizing patterns and learning what they should and should not do based on our instructions. However, collecting those vast amounts of data and the usage of AI in general comes with as many challenges as opportunities that we as a society need to consider. One advantage of AI is that it can relieve us of tedious tasks through automation. However, its use in many different areas of society also gives rise to critical problems and they are usually related to the training data. This training data consists of all kinds of human made content and without proper care, it can amplify injustices and discrimination such as racism or sexism. Since these systems cannot think for themselves, they just repeat what they receive and may reproduce the worst behaviors from humankind. The same goes for wealth inequality, if not well regulated AI can make the gap between rich and poor become even worse. That's why we need many different eyes and hands together to check how it works. These systems also need a lot of energy to work. A recent study estimated that by 2030 A I may consume more energy than all farms in the world combined. So the same tool that can help us find solutions against climate change can also make it worse by using so much energy, using A I in many areas of our society creates what people call a wicked problem with so many different perspectives involved. There's no simple solution and that's why we need a nuanced perspective. Since it can affect many areas of our lives, it's important to develop a good understanding of technology. This critical AI should be part of educational programs to empower more people to use and shape these tools for a more equal and fair society. Additionally, we need good laws for it. Our governments and private companies need clear rules so that AI can be transparent, accountable, inclusive and respect human rights. A well informed and strong civil society can help shape this technology. So it works for everyone. Some examples are clear labels to content generated by AI and holding companies accountable for their systems and training the users of these systems must also be protected. So their private and sensitive data is not misused. However, this only scratches the surface of this new technology. Go visit democracy-ai.eu and learn more about it with more videos and a free online course.
